reason: The only proposal (D-a44f2b) is about build:self scripts in package.json; it says nothing about .ts import extensions. All relative script imports use .ts (JSON imports use .json).
No proposal about import type. Scripts mark type-only names with the type modifier (e.g. `type Ownership`, `type ChildProcess`).
No proposal about dependency resolution. Node scripts import node: builtins and npm packages (yaml, @optique/*); there are no jsr: or path-alias imports, and Deno scripts are excluded.
No proposal about strip-types syntax limits. A grep finds no enum, namespace or constructor parameter properties in scripts/.
No proposal about tsconfig presets. All check configs extend node, workers or bun presets except packages/adonisjs, which extends its own tsconfig.json.
No proposal about runtime globals. Node code avoids the Deno global; lint is an explicit exception with Deno types, and runtime access is limited to files listed in the ownership file.
No proposal about declaring Deno. Runtime-neutral modules that detect Deno use a module-scope `declare const Deno: {...}` subset.
No proposal about type-check ownership. Coverage can only be confirmed by running check:types.
No proposal about strict typing. A grep finds `any` in only two exported signatures, both koa generic defaults (TKoaContext = any).
No proposal about generics. Public APIs consistently use a TContextData type parameter.
No proposal about platform APIs. Neutral packages mostly use node: builtins that all runtimes support; the few Bun/Deno-specific spots are isolated or guarded.
No proposal about FederationBuilder. Federation configuration uses fluent set*Dispatcher methods with route callbacks.
No proposal about where vocabulary lives. Vocabulary classes are generated in @fedify/vocab; fedify/src/vocab only re-exports them.
No proposal about moved directories. Only deprecated re-export shims remain in runtime/ and vocab/; codegen/ and webfinger/ are gone.
No proposal about signature verification. Object Integrity Proof verification exists and is used; legacy LD/HTTP signature paths are also kept.
No proposal about JSDoc. Most public exports have JSDoc, but some do not (e.g. the express ContextDataFactory and integrateFederation).
No proposal about naming case. Code uses no snake_case identifiers; there are about 500 SCREAMING_CASE constants against about 21.7k camelCase ones.
No proposal about acronym casing. Public exported names treat acronyms as words (e.g. UrlError style); no all-caps acronym names found apart from IPv/ITerm.
No proposal about discriminator casing. Most multi-word discriminator values are camelCase ("invalidProof", "keyFetchError"): about 62 distinct camel/snake values against 14 kebab-case.
No proposal about predicate prefixes. 14 boolean properties carry is/has prefixes against about 290 that do not.
No proposal about type naming. Only a handful of the ~890 exported types use Info/Data/Details suffixes.
No proposal about telemetry naming. Attribute keys follow OTel snake_case dotted names, and their values mirror API tags directly (e.g. reason.type).
No proposal about test stores. 65 test files use MemoryKvStore/InProcessMessageQueue; DB stores appear only in adapter or lint tests.
No proposal about the test API. Most packages use node:test, but several (nuxt, uri-template, testing, nestjs, next) use the fixture test() wrapper instead.
No proposal about the fixture test(). fedify and vocab tests import test from @fedify/fixture, not node:test.
No proposal about fixture imports. Non-test imports appear only in fedify/src/testing/* and a bench file.
No proposal about test helper reuse. 49 test files import @fedify/testing or the fedify testing helpers; a few define local mocks.
No proposal about dual dependency declaration. Shared deps appear both in deno.json imports and in package.json; full verification is not feasible statically.
No proposal about catalog refs (D-a44f2b is about build:self scripts). 263 catalog-eligible deps use catalog: and 25 copy a version string (some on purpose, as wider peer ranges).
No proposal about jsr specifiers. hono, @logtape and @optique use jsr:, but some JSR-available packages (yaml, es-toolkit) are mapped with npm:.
No proposal about init dependency versions. No hard-coded version literals in init sources outside json/.
No proposal about the deps import. Framework descriptions reference deps[...] or PACKAGE_VERSION, not literal versions.
No proposal about the repository field. Every non-private package.json has a repository field.
No proposal about tsconfig.check.json. It exists everywhere except the Deno-only denokv and fresh, and adonisjs does not extend a preset.
No proposal about workspace listing. Every npm package is in pnpm-workspace.yaml; Deno packages are in the deno.json workspace.
No proposal about JSR metadata. Every package deno.json has name and publish, and config.mts derives the package list from the workspace.
No proposal about generated vocab. vocab.ts is not committed (it is generated), and mod.ts uses `export * from ./vocab.ts` rather than hand-written exports.
No proposal about adapter layering. fedify holds only the interfaces plus in-memory implementations; DB adapters live in their own packages.
No proposal about adapter completeness. postgres, redis, sqlite, mysql, denokv, cfworkers and netlify implement both; pglite has KvStore only (amqp is MQ-only by nature).
No proposal about template comments. No template instruction comments remain in the integration packages.
No proposal about dual manifests (D-a44f2b covers only package.json scripts). Most integrations have both files; adonisjs, nestjs and next lack deno.json, and fresh lacks package.json.
No proposal about export surface. Most entry modules export only the integration function and ContextDataFactory; next and h3 export extra helpers.
No proposal about required exports. Most entry modules export a handler plus ContextDataFactory; sveltekit, fresh and next do not export ContextDataFactory.
No proposal about onNotFound. Most integrations delegate to next(); next returns a plain 404.
No proposal about onNotAcceptable. Most integrations call the framework first; next and fastify return 406 directly from the callback.
No proposal about the 406 body. Most use the exact response; hono omits the headers, and fastify and solidstart spell the body "Not Acceptable".
No proposal about request conversion. Integrations for frameworks with native request types include conversion helpers (fromERequest, toWebRequest).
No proposal about function naming. Most integrations use other names (integrateFederation, createMiddleware, federation, fedifyHook); only astro and solidstart use fedifyMiddleware.
No proposal about tsdown config (build:self is a package.json script, not the file). Every Node-capable integration has tsdown.config.ts.
No proposal about test file naming. Integration tests are all named *.test.ts.
No proposal about the integration test API. Most use node:test; nestjs, next and nuxt use the fixture test().
No proposal about runner comments. No integration package test uses vitest or another runner, so there is nothing to check.
No proposal about fixture imports. No non-test integration source imports @fedify/fixture.
No proposal about test coverage. Most integrations test JSON-LD, 406 and HTML fallthrough; sveltekit, h3 and hono lack some of the scenarios.
No proposal about framework files. Each framework has its own file that defines a WebFrameworkDescription.
No proposal about append order. The array is in non-alphabetical order, which fits appending, but insertion history cannot be seen in a snapshot.
No proposal about ordering. Entries are alphabetical except that "bare-bones" is listed first.
No proposal about templates. All 38 template files end in .tpl and sit under templates/<framework>/.
No proposal about readTemplate. Every framework description loads its files with readTemplate().
No proposal about banned lookups. BANNED_LOOKUP_REASONS holds key/reason pairs.
No proposal about examples. Few examples support both Deno and Node (astro does); most are Node-only or Deno-only.
No proposal about Hono. It is unclear which examples count as backend-only without a natural frontend.
No proposal about entry layout. Almost no example has src/main.ts plus src/app.ts; most put entry files at the root (index.ts, main.ts).
No proposal about logging. Only nuxt and rfc-9421-test have a logging.ts; most examples have none.
No proposal about host restrictions. Vite-based examples set allowedHosts; other frameworks have no such restriction.
No proposal about middleware placement. Examples have no src/app.ts; middleware is registered in root index.ts/app.ts or framework hooks.
No proposal about static assets. UI examples serve assets from public/ (sveltekit uses its framework static/ directory).
No proposal about the example registry. Every example directory is registered in mod.ts.
No proposal about middleware order. Most examples register Fedify middleware before their routes.
No proposal about x-forwarded-fetch. Only the next and sveltekit examples use getXForwardedRequest.
No proposal about the search UI. Only nuxt has handle search (through /api/search, not GET /?q=); other examples do not.
No proposal about the demo actor. Most UI examples define "Fedify Demo"; solidstart's summary differs, and backend samples use other actors.
No proposal about the post flow. nuxt does not remove the post when sending fails; sveltekit removes it but uses a different route and redirect; most examples have no POST /post.
No proposal about follow routes. Only nuxt has follow/unfollow handlers.
No proposal about SSE. Only nuxt broadcasts events; other examples change stores without SSE.
No proposal about RequestContext. Route handlers that touch federation use federation.createContext(request, ...).
No proposal about store access. Handlers do read stores directly, and whether a context method would serve each case cannot be judged statically.
No proposal about federation/store layout. No example has src/federation.ts plus src/store.ts; files sit at the root, in src/lib or in server/, and many examples have no store.ts.
No proposal about logging. Most examples lack src/logging.ts; only 10 example files import @logtape/logtape.
No proposal about themes. Most UI examples use prefers-color-scheme for dark mode.
No proposal about breakpoints. Every width media query uses 768px, but many examples have no responsive CSS.
No proposal about CSS variables. Most UI examples define --background/--foreground.

No proposal about CSS frameworks. Tailwind is used in four examples (all three next ones and sveltekit-sample).
No proposal about fonts. Two next examples load fonts; the rest use system fonts.
No proposal about client JS. The only public/*.js script (nuxt theme.js) just toggles the light/dark class.
